question: A 46-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 6-week history of fatigue and cramping abdominal pain. He works at a gun range. Examination shows pale conjunctivae and gingival hyperpigmentation. There is weakness when extending the left wrist against resistance. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lead exposure at the gun range -> Lead poisoning -> Anemia -> Pale conjunctivae and gingival hyperpigmentation -> 80% CHAIN: Lead exposure at the gun range -> Lead poisoning -> Neuromuscular symptoms -> Weakness when extending the left wrist against resistance -> 75% CHAIN: Lead exposure at the gun range -> Lead poisoning -> Basophilic stippling of erythrocytes -> Basophilic stippling of erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with fatigue, abdominal pain, pale conjunctivae, gingival hyperpigmentation, and weakness when extending the left wrist against resistance suggests a diagnosis of lead poisoning. The most likely finding on further evaluation would be basophilic stippling of erythrocytes, which is a characteristic feature of lead toxicity.
